Zimbabwe Women 19th Match, Group B Bangladesh Women vs Thailand Women 20th Match, Group B Afghanistan vs Zimbabwe in UAE, 2026 Bowlers give Zimbabwe iron grip in Sharjah after Muzarabani, Cremer fifties
 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet [File photo] © Afghanistan Cricket Board [File photo] © Afghanistan Cricket Board A handy ninth-wicket stand stretched Zimbabwe’s lead past 400 before their bowlers took out Afghanistan’s top five, pushing them into deep trouble going into the final day of the second Test in Sharjah.
 At Stumps, Afghanistan stood at 143/5, starved of a fighting partnership from their top-order. They lost their top three for 42, briefly recovering from Brad Evans’s double strike on either side of Tea. A 48-run stand between Hashmatullah Shahidi and Rahmat Shah briefly arrested the slide, but both fell to spin on a surface with increased turn on offer.
 Cremer used it to take out Rahmat, inducing an outside edge with extra bounce for Brendan Taylor to take a sharp catch. Vincent Masekesa had Innocent Kaia to thank for a sharp reflex catch at short-leg, pouching the inner edge of Shahidi’s bat. It gave them their fifth wicket, setting off wild celebrations led by Kaia, who had dropped one at the same position in the first innings.
 Afsar Zazai and Ikram Alikhil survived the last patch, batting unseparated for 11 overs, leaving Afghanistan needing 275 runs when Stumps were called. Alikhil was helped by an incorrect call from the umpire when on 10. A clear inside-edge, caught at forward short-leg, wasn’t given out. Alikhil was later also hit on the helmet by a Muzarabani snorter but stayed on. Subsequently, under receding light, Zimbabwe were asked to stick to spin for the last two overs.
 Cremer and Blessing Muzarabani had a different role to play earlier in the day. Resuming on 169/7, Zimbabwe’s primary motive was to extend their lead, which stood at 291 overnight. Fifties from the duo meant that they ended up with a lot more than they would've expected. Cremer finished not out on 50, his first fifty-plus Test score since a century against Sri Lanka in Harare ten years ago.
 For Muzarabani, it was his first time breaching fifty in Tests. He hit ten fours and a six as Zimbabwe’s lead grew in the morning, thumping his chest before raising his bat to celebrate the milestone. He was out slogging to be their ninth wicket. Not too long after, Cremer ticked past his fifty too, prompting a declaration, and setting Afghanistan a target of 418.
 Afghanistan’s response was dealt an early blow as Abdul Malik fell in the second over, nicking behind to Brad Evans after crunching a four off him the previous ball. As Zimbabwe celebrated, Malik stood transfixed, reluctantly heading back for his third single-digit score in the last four innings.
 Rahmanullah was sucked into a short-ball trap, getting a top-edge off an attempted pull to Muzarabani, with fine-leg and deep square-leg stationed. The reaction from bowling coach Hamid Hassan, head down in disappointment, said it all.
 Evans struck again five balls into the final session, getting Sediqullah Atal to push at a ball outside off. Shahidi and Rahmat, their batting pillars, then steadied the innings, but spin first teased then trapped them, leaving Afghanistan with their backs against the wall ahead of the final day.
 Brief scores: Afghanistan 217 & 143/5 (Hashmatullah Shahidi 35, Rahmat Shah 30; Brad Evans 2-25, Blessing Muzarabani 1-24) trail Zimbabwe 339 & 295/9 declared (Blessing Muzarabani 59, Graeme Cremer 50; Saleem Safi 3-78, Yamin Ahmadzai 2-44) by 274 runs.
